title: Pediatric Pulmonology Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (independent self-study curriculum; not an actual fellowship)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Licensed physician or senior pediatric trainee background is assumed for advanced-level study; no learner status is verified.
Prior pediatrics, physiology, pharmacology, microbiology, evidence appraisal and basic pulmonary function testing are recommended.
Educational self-study only; clinical application requires formal training, supervision, institutional policies, and current clinician judgment.
objectives: Map respiratory symptoms to developmentally informed differential diagnoses.
Interpret pulmonary tests and identify their technical limitations.
Apply current authoritative sources to pediatric asthma, infection, CF, neonatal, sleep, chronic failure, ILD, vascular and systemic disorders.
Appraise clinical evidence and articulate diagnostic uncertainty, equity and safety considerations.
Understand the boundaries between a didactic blueprint and accredited clinical fellowship competence/eligibility.

units.title: Developmental lung biology, mechanics, and gas exchange
objectives: Relate alveolar, airway, and vascular development to age-dependent physiology.
Interpret oxygenation, ventilation, mechanics, and age-adjusted physiology at a conceptual level.
Explain how prematurity and growth affect respiratory reserve.
topics: Embryologic lung development; airway branching/alveolarization; surfactant; compliance/resistance; V/Q; control of breathing; normal maturation.
Developmental physiology across infancy and childhood; reserve and maturation remain under-covered by the linked recordings.
units.casePractice: Fictional age-stratified physiology worksheet; no real patient data.
units.assessment: Short-answer causal map (development → mechanics → measured function), rubric: physiology 40%, age-aware interpretation 30%, limits/uncertainty 30%.

units.title: Symptoms, history, examination, and diagnostic reasoning
objectives: Structure a developmentally appropriate respiratory history and focused exam.
Generate and rank a broad differential for cough, wheeze, stridor, dyspnea, hypoxemia, clubbing, and hemoptysis.
Choose tests based on pretest probability and acknowledge limits.
topics: Noisy breathing localization; chronic cough; recurrent pneumonia; dyspnea; clubbing; hypoxemia; red flags; shared decisions and equity.
Congenital and acquired airway/lung malformations; structural disease patterns and age-aware localization.
units.casePractice: ATS interactive case catalog is link-out only; compare alternate explanations without copying case images.
units.assessment: Differential/diagnostic-test matrix scored for breadth, discriminating features, test choice, safety-net and uncertainty.

units.title: Neonatal and infant lung disease; BPD
objectives: Differentiate common neonatal respiratory phenotypes from unusual or progressive disease.
Describe BPD as an evolving clinical construct and evaluate longitudinal respiratory support context.
Critically appraise evidence without converting a single study into a universal treatment rule.
topics: RDS, apnea, BPD, airway malacia, infant respiratory distress, chronic lung disease of prematurity, neonatal pulmonary function and follow-up.
Bronchopulmonary dysplasia as an evolving developmental lung disorder; evidence interpretation and longitudinal outcomes.
units.casePractice: ATS pediatric clinical case lectures plus fictional longitudinal BPD vignette; no patient images are copied.
units.assessment: Evidence table comparing population, outcome, bias and applicability; 4-point rubric for appraisal.

units.title: Asthma across childhood: diagnosis, control, and difficult disease
objectives: Distinguish asthma from mimics, particularly when age limits objective testing.
Classify impairment/risk/control using a named current guideline and state its publication date.
Analyze adherence, technique, exposures, comorbidity, phenotype, and escalation options before labeling refractory disease.
topics: Preschool wheeze; spirometry/bronchodilator response; exacerbation prevention; action plans; severe asthma; biologics; disparities and access.
Severe asthma phenotyping and escalation as a specialist reasoning topic; verify all medication indications against current guidance.
units.casePractice: Fictional preschool recurrent-wheeze and school-age poor-control vignettes; no dosing protocol.
units.assessment: Write diagnostic uncertainty, modifiable factors, safety plan and guideline version. Rubric: evidence/currentness 35%, differential 25%, equity/access 20%, communication 20%.

units.title: Respiratory infections, immunity, and atypical pneumonia
objectives: Use age, host status, epidemiology, and tempo to organize infectious differentials.
Select microbiology/imaging thoughtfully and distinguish colonization from invasive infection.
Explain infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship.
topics: Viral bronchiolitis/RSV, pneumonia, TB, fungal disease, opportunistic infection, immunocompromise, unusual infection patterns.
Immunodeficiency-associated respiratory disorders; complicated pneumonia; host context; non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM).
units.casePractice: ATS cases with linked public discussion; constructed differential exercises only.
units.assessment: One-page diagnostic stewardship analysis; rubric: differential 30%, test utility 30%, stewardship 25%, uncertainty 15%.

units.title: Cystic fibrosis and non-CF bronchiectasis
objectives: Explain CF diagnostic pathways and uncertainty around screen-positive/inconclusive states.
Integrate airway infection, clearance, nutrition, multisystem disease, modulators and transition.
Compare bronchiectasis etiologies and recognize when to investigate underlying causes.
topics: CFTR disease; sweat testing/newborn screen; CRMS/CFSPID; microbiology; exacerbations; airway clearance; NTM; CFTR modulators; non-CF bronchiectasis.
Primary ciliary dyskinesia; non-CF bronchiectasis differential; pediatric CF didactics; multiple-breath washout; NTM.
units.casePractice: ATS CF clinical case presentation; link only. CFF guidelines are clinician resources; care at accredited center remains essential.
units.assessment: Create phenotype→confirmatory test→differential map; rubric: diagnostic criteria 40%, multisystem scope 25%, infection/control context 20%, limits 15%.

units.title: Neuromuscular disease, aspiration, and respiratory muscle weakness
objectives: Recognize respiratory muscle weakness and impaired cough/airway clearance.
Distinguish hypoventilation, aspiration, obstructive disease and infection in complex patients.
Describe interdisciplinary evaluation and the limits of non-clinical learning for device decisions.
topics: Neuromuscular disorders; swallowing/aspiration; cough effectiveness; sleep-related hypoventilation; transition planning.
Core content remains mostly represented by public case-based material and does not amount to comprehensive specialty teaching.
units.casePractice: Fictional scenario, learner identifies consult questions but does not prescribe settings.
units.assessment: Concept map plus escalation/consult plan; rubric: mechanism 35%, diagnostic plan 35%, scope/safety 30%.

units.title: Chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and home ventilation
objectives: Classify acute-on-chronic respiratory failure and integrate gas exchange/clinical trajectory.
Describe equipment classes and safety/family-system considerations for chronic support.
Explain multidisciplinary discharge, monitoring, emergency planning and transition processes.
topics: Oxygen, noninvasive ventilation, tracheostomy, home ventilators, weaning evidence, respiratory technology, airway clearance, goals of care.
Technology-dependent child; pediatric sleep teaching; interpret modalities in age-specific context and avoid extrapolating adult testing pathways.
units.casePractice: Fictional family-centered device safety case; no actual settings or patient records.
units.assessment: Discharge safety checklist design, evaluated for interprofessional coordination, contingency planning, and explicit non-prescriptive limits.

units.title: Pulmonary diagnostics, bronchoscopy, and function testing
objectives: Interpret spirometry, lung volumes, DLCO, exercise tests and sleep studies with quality limitations.
Recognize when bronchoscopy/imaging are indicated and their risks/alternatives.
Distinguish educational interpretation from independently performing procedures.
topics: Spirometry; flow-volume loops; lung volumes; gas transfer; oscillometry/EIT; exercise; bronchoscopy; imaging principles; test quality.
Congenital airway/lung anomaly evaluation; multiple-breath washout; pediatric sleep diagnostic methods.
units.casePractice: Use public ATS educational talks; do not reproduce endoscopy clips/images without permission.
units.assessment: Annotated hypothetical spirometry report and test-selection OSCE prompt; 4-point rubric for technical quality, pattern, differential, caveats.

units.title: Diffuse/restrictive lung disease, pulmonary vascular and systemic disease
objectives: Construct a staged evaluation for childhood interstitial/diffuse lung disease and pulmonary vascular disease.
Recognize lung manifestations of systemic disease, cancer therapy, congenital heart disease, and immune dysregulation.
Avoid premature diagnosis; identify multidisciplinary consultation and urgent threats.
topics: chILD, restrictive physiology, pulmonary hypertension, lymphatic disease, plastic bronchitis, sickle cell, autoimmune and cancer-related pulmonary effects.
Childhood ILD, immunodeficiency and lung disease associated with rheumatologic conditions; pediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension.
units.casePractice: Link to recorded case teaching; no reproduction of images or patient materials.
units.assessment: Compare broad differential and select next diagnostic categories; rubric: completeness 30%, discriminating evidence 30%, urgency 20%, uncertainty 20%.

units.title: Environmental, occupational, and exertional respiratory stress
objectives: Identify exposures and environmental determinants relevant to pediatric respiratory symptoms.
Explain respiratory stress during exercise, altitude, infection and environmental injury.
Incorporate household/school context, prevention, and health equity.
topics: Smoke/vaping, pollution/climate, secondhand exposures, exercise-induced symptoms, acute lung injury, environmental justice.
The recorded sessions introduce pulmonary hypertension and systemic lung disease; full physiology, environmental injury and longitudinal risk assessment remain topic needs.
units.casePractice: Learner designs fictional exposure history; no personal health data.
units.assessment: Exposure map and prevention memo; rubric: exposure specificity 30%, causal uncertainty 25%, feasible prevention 25%, equity lens 20%.

units.title: Evidence appraisal, scholarship, transitions, ethics, and board integration
objectives: Translate ABP domains into a self-directed review plan without treating blueprint weights as competence certification.
Appraise an intervention study for population, comparator, outcomes, bias and applicability.
Discuss transition, shared decisions, professionalism, health equity, and research ethics.
topics: ABP content outline; study appraisal; quality improvement; scholarly activity; transition; safety culture; equity; ethics; educational assessment.
Lung transplantation overview; recorded sessions inform context but do not confer transplant-team competence.
units.casePractice: Use constructed cases and public links; never claim ABP endorsement or predictive pass score.
units.assessment: Portfolio: 19-domain gap map, evidence appraisal, reflective uncertainty log. Rubric: evidence quality 30%, balanced reasoning 25%, relevance 25%, ethical/equity context 20%.

assignment.title: Longitudinal case reasoning and evidence portfolio
assignment.description: For each of 12 units, submit a one-page fictional case problem representation, age-aware differential, proposed question-driven diagnostic strategy, one guideline/version check, and reflection on uncertainty, equity and safety. Final portfolio includes board-domain self-map and a journal-club critique. Do not use patient records, protected exam content, copied case images or individual treatment plans.

rubric.performance: Accurately structured, age/context-aware; alternatives and uncertainty explicit.
Uses authoritative source, verifies date/version, distinguishes evidence from local protocol.
Tests linked to a question, technical/benefit-harm caveats stated.
Developmentally appropriate, family/system context and escalation needs considered.
No real PHI, copying without permission or claims of authorization/competency.

assessment.format: Self-study only; 10 original practice questions in this course file; unit assignments are formative.
assessment.note: No validated summative exam, standard setting, psychometric validation, official ABP content, predicted pass score or ABP endorsement. Learner performance is not credentialing.

studyHours.planBreakdown: 12 units × 10 hours = 120 hours; 30 hours assignments/cases; 20 hours question review and error log; 10 hours longitudinal revision. This is a transparent learner study plan, not observed/official BCH didactic time, clinical training time, or predicted readiness.

unitMap.text: Developmental lung biology, mechanics, and gas exchange
coveredTopics: Embryologic lung development; airway branching/alveolarization; surfactant; compliance/resistance; V/Q; control of breathing; normal maturation.
Developmental physiology across infancy and childhood; reserve and maturation remain under-covered by the linked recordings.

unitMap.text: Symptoms, history, examination, and diagnostic reasoning
coveredTopics: Noisy breathing localization; chronic cough; recurrent pneumonia; dyspnea; clubbing; hypoxemia; red flags; shared decisions and equity.
Congenital and acquired airway/lung malformations; structural disease patterns and age-aware localization.

unitMap.text: Neonatal and infant lung disease; BPD
coveredTopics: RDS, apnea, BPD, airway malacia, infant respiratory distress, chronic lung disease of prematurity, neonatal pulmonary function and follow-up.
Bronchopulmonary dysplasia as an evolving developmental lung disorder; evidence interpretation and longitudinal outcomes.

unitMap.text: Asthma across childhood: diagnosis, control, and difficult disease
coveredTopics: Preschool wheeze; spirometry/bronchodilator response; exacerbation prevention; action plans; severe asthma; biologics; disparities and access.
Severe asthma phenotyping and escalation as a specialist reasoning topic; verify all medication indications against current guidance.

unitMap.text: Respiratory infections, immunity, and atypical pneumonia
coveredTopics: Viral bronchiolitis/RSV, pneumonia, TB, fungal disease, opportunistic infection, immunocompromise, unusual infection patterns.
Immunodeficiency-associated respiratory disorders; complicated pneumonia; host context; non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM).

unitMap.text: Cystic fibrosis and non-CF bronchiectasis
coveredTopics: CFTR disease; sweat testing/newborn screen; CRMS/CFSPID; microbiology; exacerbations; airway clearance; NTM; CFTR modulators; non-CF bronchiectasis.
Primary ciliary dyskinesia; non-CF bronchiectasis differential; pediatric CF didactics; multiple-breath washout; NTM.

unitMap.text: Neuromuscular disease, aspiration, and respiratory muscle weakness
coveredTopics: Neuromuscular disorders; swallowing/aspiration; cough effectiveness; sleep-related hypoventilation; transition planning.

topicGaps: The external-recording floor is met by unique, publicly listed ATS recordings (37.39 observed hours); this total is an inventory of viewing time, not a complete fellowship didactic course, rendered original teaching, clinical training, competence, credit, or board readiness.

Substantial source-backed video depth is still uneven: core developmental lung biology/mechanics and pediatric pulmonary physiology; test-quality interpretation across spirometry, lung volumes, DLCO, exercise and bronchoscopy; control-of-breathing physiology; pulmonary vascular/lymphatic and systemic disease decision frameworks; environmental respiratory stress and health equity; and rigorous evidence appraisal remain insufficiently covered as an integrated course.

The added 2019/2020 ATS symposium sessions are freely viewable recordings but not necessarily current clinical guidance. Use current authoritative guidance for every evolving diagnostic criterion, drug indication, monitoring strategy and clinical decision.

The public fellowship page and ACGME 2021 PDF do not disclose BCH protected didactics or their exact hours; current institutional accreditation status and current ACGME requirement revision must be independently confirmed.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 4-year-old has episodic wheeze only with viral illnesses and cannot perform reliable spirometry. Which statement best reflects diagnostic reasoning?

options.text: Asthma is excluded because spirometry is unavailable.
History, pattern, examination and longitudinal response may inform assessment, while mimics and uncertainty remain important.
Any wheeze during a cold proves persistent asthma.
A smartphone recording independently confirms asthma.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NHLBI notes spirometry is often not feasible under age six; history/symptoms and longitudinal assessment may help, but viral wheeze is not itself definitive. Consider alternative diagnoses and reassess over time.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the ABP pediatric pulmonology pathway?

options.text: Completion of an online self-study course confers eligibility.
A separate ABP subspecialty certification examination exists, with required accredited fellowship training, verified competence/scholarly activity and passing the exam.
There is no pediatric pulmonary board examination.
Any three years of research-only work qualify.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABP requires three years full-time broad-based fellowship training in an ACGME-accredited US or RCPSC-accredited Canadian programme, training verification, scholarly activity and passing the subspecialty exam; exact criteria can change.

practiceQuestions.stem: A child with a positive newborn CF screen but intermediate/uncertain diagnostic testing is being discussed. Which approach is most appropriate for a learning exercise?

options.text: Label CF based solely on screening result.
Use a guideline-based diagnostic pathway and preserve inconclusive status while arranging specialist follow-up.
Assume all CFTR variants have identical clinical effect.
Avoid confirmatory testing if symptoms are absent.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Screening is not the same as a confirmed diagnosis. The CFF guideline set separately addresses diagnosis and CRMS/CFSPID; follow current specialist guidance and avoid overcalling.

practiceQuestions.stem: An infant with RSV bronchiolitis has worsening work of breathing and poor intake. What is the safest board-style framing?

options.text: All RSV requires antibiotics.
Assess severity and hydration/oxygenation, provide supportive care as indicated, and escalate based on clinical status.
RSV is only a mild upper respiratory infection in infants.
An educational module can specify individualized oxygen settings.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC describes RSV lower respiratory illness including bronchiolitis and pneumonia in children; some hospitalized infants require supportive oxygen, hydration or ventilation. Decisions require clinical assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a child with chronic wet cough, recurrent lower respiratory infections and clubbing, which broad reasoning step is strongest?

options.text: Assume asthma and stop evaluation.
Consider bronchiectasis and investigate an underlying cause, guided by history, cultures and specialist evaluation.
Clubbing proves cystic fibrosis.
Order repeated imaging without considering radiation exposure.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Chronic suppurative airway disease and bronchiectasis have multiple etiologies; CF is one possible underlying condition, not pathognomonic. Use targeted evaluation and weigh test harms.

practiceQuestions.stem: A sleep study is proposed for a child with suspected sleep-related breathing disorder. What should the learner verify?

options.text: That adult HSAT pathways always apply in children.
Age-appropriate indication, test type, technical quality and current pediatric guidance.
That symptoms alone provide the same information as PSG.
That one historic recommendation applies indefinitely.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AASM’s guideline index includes pediatric respiratory PSG-specific recommendations; distinguish pediatric from adult pathways and check currency and technical context.

practiceQuestions.stem: A child with neuromuscular weakness develops morning headaches and weak cough. Which mechanism deserves attention?

options.text: Possible hypoventilation and impaired airway clearance, among other causes.
Asthma is proven by morning headache.
A normal daytime oxygen saturation excludes nocturnal hypoventilation.
Home ventilator settings can be selected from a self-study quiz.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Neuromuscular weakness may impair ventilation and cough/secretions. Assessment is multidisciplinary and cannot be replaced by this course or a single daytime measure.

practiceQuestions.stem: When interpreting an ABP content outline, what is true of its domain weights?

options.text: They guarantee exact proportions on every form and establish a passing threshold.
They are approximate proportions for exam content; they do not validate a learner or guarantee success.
They are hospital rotation requirements.
They remain fixed forever.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABP states weights are approximate and actual proportions may vary; the blueprint is not a passing score or a training curriculum.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fellowship website publishes example rotations and says the programme is designed to meet certification criteria. Does that alone establish the programme’s current ACGME accreditation status?

options.text: Yes, an institutional description automatically proves current ACGME status.
No; confirm status through authoritative current accreditation/program directory records.
Yes, if the programme is at a famous institution.
It proves all trainees are board eligible.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Programme marketing/curriculum pages and accreditor records have different evidentiary roles. Public BCH page reviewed here did not explicitly display status.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which best describes this independent Med school curriculum?

options.text: Accredited fellowship equivalent with procedural competence.
Independent learning only; no affiliation, accredited clinical training, licensure, board eligibility or procedure authorization.
Guaranteed ABP exam preparation.
A substitute for direct supervision and patient care.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Self-study cannot replace medical education, accredited training, clinical supervision, case/procedure experience, licensure or certifying-board eligibility and cannot guarantee exam performance.

officialProgrammes.name: Pediatric Regional Anesthesia
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official BCH directory (checked 2026-10-07) lists ACGME Accredited: NO; prerequisite pediatric anesthesia fellowship or adult regional anesthesia fellowship; fellowship length 6 months to 1 year; 2026–27 and 2027–28 accepting applications yes; diploma awarded. Official page separately describes optional two-year sequence: one-year ACGME core pediatric anesthesiology plus an advanced subspecialty year. That combined sequence is distinct from the regional fellowship alone. ASRA’s institution-submitted directory labels the fellowship non-ACGME and lists 12 months, so duration is preserved as a source discrepancy rather than harmonized.

medical.programmeSourceScope: One physician clinical advanced fellowship only. It is not a generic fellowship-directory category, not the ACGME pediatric anesthesiology fellowship, and not a research/non-physician supplement. No other institutional variant was identified in the supplied packet. Exact official institutional variant preserved as Boston Children’s Hospital “Pediatric Regional Anesthesia.” ASRA directory identifies BCH as a Harvard Medical School teaching hospital. This is not a Harvard/Johns Hopkins-sponsored course.
sourceCaveats: BCH source lists fellowship length 6 months to 1 year; ASRA institution-supplied listing says 12 months. Both exact institutional descriptions preserved; no independent harmonization.
The ABA Pediatric Anesthesiology exam is not a Pediatric Regional Anesthesia board exam. Regional fellowship is listed non-ACGME; do not infer ABA exam eligibility from this programme.
The ACGME Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine requirements are a comparator, not the programme’s accreditation standard.

topicGaps: The 36-hour free-recording target remains unmet: 2.9269 conservative specialty hours from two public time-coded recording transcripts are counted; 33.0731 hours remain.

The two counted durations are last-spoken transcript timestamps, not native player total runtimes; silent tails and direct playback were not independently verified. Counted values are conservative floors only.
Coverage is concentrated in broad pediatric regional block and neonatal/infant webinar content; no complete public specialty lecture series or full institutional didactic curriculum was located.

Units 1, 10 and 12 have no qualifying external recording mapped; unit 3 has no dedicated verified current pediatric pharmacology recording; unit 7 lacks a full acute-pain service and follow-up recording.
The 2018 pediatric local-anesthetic advisory and older neuraxial review are educational sources, not current local dose references or procedural instructions; current clinical review is required.
The PRAN registry papers were reviewed only through their publicly accessible abstracts; full-text methods/tables and local applicability remain to be verified before detailed numerical reuse.

Remaining public candidates have unresolved runtime or access (including caudal video listings, the historical lecture listing, the CSurgeries page, and the closed ASRA webinar page); they remain uncounted.
The four authored episodes are complete scripts marked scripted only. They have not been rendered, duration-probed, uploaded, or reviewed by a qualified clinician, and contribute zero video hours.

The ABA blueprint says eligibility is tied to successful completion of an ACGME-accredited pediatric anesthesiology fellowship.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the best interpretation of a published pediatric local-anesthetic dose advisory?

options.text: It is an individualized prescription for all children
It eliminates the need to account for concurrent blocks
It offers guidance but evidence is limited and clinical context/current local policy remain necessary
It certifies a learner to perform blocks

practiceQuestions.rationale: The joint advisory describes limited high-level evidence and variability; it is not an individualized order or competence credential.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the strongest inference from a clear ultrasound image during a regional procedure?

options.text: Correct placement and safe injection are proven
The image provides anatomical information but does not alone prove correct placement or safety
All pediatric anatomy is visible
A complication is impossible

practiceQuestions.rationale: Imaging can inform anatomy and needle visualization but is not proof of correct placement, spread, or safety.

practiceQuestions.stem: What should a learner do when a question describes possible local anesthetic systemic toxicity?

options.text: Rely on recalled details from a teaching video
Locate the current ASRA checklist and follow institutional emergency response
Continue the planned study task
Use a generic adult algorithm without checking

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASRA offers a public LAST checklist and advises clinicians to be prepared. Current versions and local emergency systems should be checked.

practiceQuestions.stem: The ABA Pediatric Anesthesiology exam blueprint lists regional anesthesia under which broad content category?

options.text: Basic Sciences
Clinical Science of Anesthesia
Special Problems only
Clinical Subspecialties only

practiceQuestions.rationale: The published blueprint lists “Regional Anesthesia & Analgesia” within Clinical Science of Anesthesia.

practiceQuestions.stem: An open-access case report contains ultrasound images. What is appropriate for this course?

options.text: Download and insert the image in course notes without checking rights
Link to the article, discuss the published case at a high level, and verify license before any reproduction
Assume open access means unrestricted commercial reuse
Crop out the watermark and rehost

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free-to-view does not imply reuse rights; article terms and image-specific conditions must be checked. This course stores no patient images.

practiceQuestions.stem: A student finishes this independent curriculum. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: They may independently perform pediatric regional anesthesia
They are board eligible for pediatric anesthesiology
They completed an educational self-study only; no procedure competence or eligibility is conferred
They completed ACGME training

practiceQuestions.rationale: Independent education is not accredited training, supervised experience, licensure, board eligibility, certification, or procedural competence.

practiceQuestions.stem: Why should pediatric age and developmental status be included in pharmacologic risk reasoning?

options.text: They never affect local anesthetic exposure
Developmental physiology can alter binding, distribution, and clearance, while evidence remains imperfect
Only adult weight matters
Age matters only for ultrasound image quality

practiceQuestions.rationale: Developmental pharmacology and age-related risk are discussed in the joint ESRA/ASRA advisory. Specific dosing must be obtained from current qualified references, not inferred here.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the best next question in a fictional postoperative analgesia vignette before selecting a technique?

options.text: Which technique is most fashionable?
What pain territory/time course, alternatives, child-specific factors, monitoring, and rescue pathway are relevant?
How can we avoid documentation?
Can one procedure suit every child?

practiceQuestions.rationale: Safe decision-making starts with the clinical problem, alternatives, patient factors, and monitoring/rescue capability rather than technique preference.

title: Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship curriculum (independent self-study; not clinical training)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Physician learners who have completed, or are enrolled after, accredited PM&R residency; senior residents/fellows are the intended audience.
Working familiarity with pediatric neurodevelopment, neurologic and musculoskeletal examination, rehabilitation team roles, and evidence appraisal.
This course does not establish medical licensure, credentialing, a clinician-patient relationship, or authorization to provide care.
objectives: Use the current ABPMR PRM Examination Outline as a curriculum map, including all six weighted domains.
Analyze function, participation, developmental context and family-defined goals in fictional educational scenarios.
Compare public institutional PRM programme descriptions with ACGME requirements and ABPMR eligibility without conflating them.
Apply current, source-linked guidance cautiously to CP, spina bifida, SCI/TBI, neuromuscular and musculoskeletal learning cases.
Critically describe uncertainty and appropriate team/referral boundaries.

units.title: PRM framework: function, participation, and outcomes
objectives: Distinguish impairment, activity, participation, environmental and personal factors in ICF terms.
Construct a person- and family-defined functional problem list and measurable goal set.
Select an outcome measure appropriate to developmental level and intended decision.
topics: PRM scope; developmental stage; family-centered interviewing; function-focused exam; PROMs and performance measures; longitudinal outcomes.

units.title: Development, early detection, and differential diagnosis

units.title: Cerebral palsy and lifelong function
objectives: Describe CP motor phenotype and associated impairments without conflating nonprogressive brain lesion with changing secondary consequences.

topics: CP definition and phenotypes; GMFCS/MACS/CFCS concepts; early intervention; hip and bone surveillance; transition and adult care; evidence levels.
boardDomains: Brain disorders (30%): cerebral palsy; traumatic/nonaccidental; anoxic; stroke; infectious; inflammatory/demyelinating; degenerative

units.title: Tone, dystonia, and evidence-informed interventions

units.title: Neuromuscular, genetic, and congenital conditions
objectives: Build a differential across neuropathy, plexopathy, NMJ, myopathy and motor-neuron patterns.

topics: DMD/SMA/high-level overview; arthrogryposis; Down syndrome; rare disease; fatigue and contracture; respiratory/cardiac surveillance coordination; genetic diagnosis boundaries.

units.casePractice: CasePractice: Sort fictional weakness patterns by localization and list next data/referrals, not a definitive diagnosis.

assignment.title: Integrated pediatric rehabilitation case conference and service-improvement brief
assignment.directions: Using only the explicitly fictional case vignette provided within a unit or the linked, lawfully accessible and de-identified published case report, submit (1) an ICF-informed functional formulation; (2) a child/family-prioritized goal set; (3) a source-mapped differential and surveillance/referral questions; (4) a one-page evidence table distinguishing recommendations, evidence certainty and local confirmation needed; and (5) a service-level QI aim with measure and equity safeguard. Do not give real-patient treatment advice, copy protected images, or propose unsupervised procedures.
assignment.completionThreshold: 80/100 is a course-design mastery threshold only; it does not predict board success or clinical competence.

assessment.format: Low-stakes retrieval questions, 12 unit assignments, final integrated case/QI brief and reflective review.
assessment.passingInterpretation: Self-study completion only; no validated prediction of ABPMR performance. Questions are original educational items, not official ABPMR content.
rubricPrinciples: Explain reasoning and uncertainty, not merely answer selection.
Separate a fictional educational scenario from patient advice.
Avoid overclaiming effect, diagnosis, eligibility or procedural competence.

topicGaps: 32.078611 verified hours remain below the 36-hour floor (36 target minus 3.921389 counted hours); no future recording, planned runtime, or portal listing is counted.

Recording coverage remains concentrated in cerebral palsy; the four new sources are three CP-focused sessions and one assistive-technology session. AACPDM/UCTV/Boston videos are supplemental and neither constitute a comprehensive PRM course nor substitute for the weighted ABPMR outline.

Insufficient verified instructional recordings remain for spinal cord disorders (neural tube defects, pediatric SCI, tethering and syrinx); neuromuscular/genetic disorders; broad musculoskeletal, limb difference/amputation and rheumatic disease; pediatric cancer; pain/functional syndromes/orthostatic intolerance; and growth/development.

The AAPM&R archive/2025 courses still lack public player/runtime evidence and available access was not verified without portal entry; UCSF's CP provider video remains duration-unknown. Both remain excluded.

P01-P35 are source pointers and future production shells in the source packet, not full authored recordings. Four original episodes are scripted in the companion artifact; none is rendered, recorded, clinically reviewed, or counted toward verified hours.

The 32.078611-hour remainder is a real access/coverage gap, not a production or exam-readiness estimate. A comprehensive production and clinical-review schedule is undetermined; do not claim feasibility or fill the deficit with repeated, short, or off-topic video.

medical.boardEligibilityNotice: ABPMR requires current diplomate status in good standing and an unrestricted license plus one of its specified training pathways: two years ACGME-accredited PRM fellowship after PM&R residency; PM&R/pediatrics combined training; or consecutive PM&R and pediatrics residencies including at least six months PRM. medical.programmeSourceScope: This specialty packet concerns physician pediatric rehabilitation medicine, not generic pediatric therapy, a non-physician rehabilitation supplement, or a research-only postdoctoral category. Preserve Hopkins/KKI and MGB/Spaulding/Harvard/BCH variants independently. Both official sources identify ACGME-accredited PRM fellowship; ACGME requires a 24-month PRM educational programme. Hopkins public page describes 1- or 2-year pathways based on prior experience and board pathway; its detailed page and individual applicant eligibility require direct confirmation. Spaulding publishes a 2-year curriculum and identifies sites. ACGME education and ABPMR eligibility are distinct.
sourceCaveats: Only two substantive specialty public videos were confirmed with visible runtime and direct free viewing. Combined duration is 5,916 seconds (1.643333 hours); lecture minutes are not estimates.
No foundation videos counted. A third UCSF video has no accessible duration; AAPM&R shows free listing but recording access requires portal path/login and runtimes were not visible. Both excluded.
RNOH has verified 3:42 but it is a short service-pathway orientation, categorized supplementary and excluded.
No full official Hopkins/KKI or Spaulding lecture set was publicly documented; published web rotation schedules are not equivalent to full lectures.
The 2021 ACGME requirements PDF was the official accessible source; current programme accreditation status and precise local curriculum can change. Confirm at ACGME ADS and programme contacts.

Board and programme eligibility are not identical. The Hopkins public page describes a 1–2-year pathway, while the ACGME PRM programme requirement is 24 months and ABPMR lists specified eligibility routes. Individual routes require board/program confirmation.

The ABPMR public outline document was parsed and its weighted domains mapped. The 2025 practice-analysis publication confirms six domains/22 subdomains for 2023–24 exams. It does not imply this course reproduces questions.
Clinical references have differing dates and some AACPDM pathways explicitly marked for update; check the live source before clinical application. No clinical review performed.

topicGaps: 32.078611 verified hours remain below the 36-hour floor (36 target minus 3.921389 counted hours); no future recording, planned runtime, or portal listing is counted.

Recording coverage remains concentrated in cerebral palsy; the four new sources are three CP-focused sessions and one assistive-technology session. AACPDM/UCTV/Boston videos are supplemental and neither constitute a comprehensive PRM course nor substitute for the weighted ABPMR outline.

Insufficient verified instructional recordings remain for spinal cord disorders (neural tube defects, pediatric SCI, tethering and syrinx); neuromuscular/genetic disorders; broad musculoskeletal, limb difference/amputation and rheumatic disease; pediatric cancer; pain/functional syndromes/orthostatic intolerance; and growth/development.

The AAPM&R archive/2025 courses still lack public player/runtime evidence and available access was not verified without portal entry; UCSF's CP provider video remains duration-unknown. Both remain excluded.

P01-P35 are source pointers and future production shells in the source packet, not full authored recordings. Four original episodes are scripted in the companion artifact; none is rendered, recorded, clinically reviewed, or counted toward verified hours.

The 32.078611-hour remainder is a real access/coverage gap, not a production or exam-readiness estimate. A comprehensive production and clinical-review schedule is undetermined; do not claim feasibility or fill the deficit with repeated, short, or off-topic video.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A preterm infant is being followed for motor concerns. Which approach best reflects the AACPDM early-detection pathway?

options.text: Use a single abnormal observation to establish a final diagnosis
Combine age-appropriate standardized assessment and clinical examination, consider neuroimaging where appropriate, and communicate the limits of the evidence
Wait until school age because early assessment is not useful
Use a motor score without considering corrected age or context

practiceQuestions.rationale: The pathway describes age-dependent combinations of standardized assessments and neuroimaging, emphasizes clinical context, and makes some recommendations conditional. No single result independently replaces evaluation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A child has a static early brain injury and worsening crouched gait with growth. Which statement is most accurate?

options.text: The diagnosis must be progressive if gait changes
A non-progressive brain disturbance is compatible with evolving secondary musculoskeletal and functional consequences
CP excludes new orthopedic problems
Function must remain constant after diagnosis

practiceQuestions.rationale: Non-progressive describes the causative disturbance, not every secondary manifestation across growth. Evaluate changing function and consider appropriate specialty assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the most appropriate use of a functional classification system in CP?

options.text: A complete individual prognosis and treatment prescription
A shared descriptor of a defined functional construct, supplemented by individual goals and context
A substitute for asking the child about participation
A measure of lesion progression

practiceQuestions.rationale: Classification can improve communication about a defined domain, but does not replace individualized assessment, goals, or family/child priorities.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which intervention principle is best supported by an open systematic review of CP motor rehabilitation?

options.text: Use passive modality-only treatment for all children
Set individualized, developmentally appropriate goals and use active task/goal-directed practice while tracking outcomes
Recommend one identical high-intensity program regardless of preferences
Assume all gross-motor approaches have high-certainty evidence

practiceQuestions.rationale: Review supports individualized, active, goal- and task-oriented motor approaches; strength of evidence varies by intervention and outcome.

practiceQuestions.stem: A child with spina bifida develops a new change in lower-limb strength and bladder function. Which learning response is safest?

options.text: Assume expected growth and defer review
Treat this as a change warranting prompt assessment by the relevant clinical team, including consideration of tethering or other causes
Diagnose tethered cord without examination
Change bladder management based only on a self-study course

practiceQuestions.rationale: New neurologic or bladder changes can be clinically important; prompt professional evaluation is appropriate. The course cannot diagnose the cause.

practiceQuestions.stem: For a published single case report about infant SCI, what is the strongest educational use?

options.text: Generalize the intervention as standard care for all infants
Critically appraise goals, context, methods and limits, then compare with broader evidence
Copy the case figures into a public course without permission
Use it to infer population-level effectiveness

practiceQuestions.rationale: Single-case reports provide detailed context but cannot establish general effectiveness; reuse rights for figures must be checked.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about tone terminology is sound?

options.text: Spasticity, dystonia and contracture are synonyms
Differentiate tone phenomenology and fixed range restriction; mixed findings may coexist
Any increased resistance to passive movement proves spasticity
A tone label alone determines an intervention

practiceQuestions.rationale: Examination and interpretation distinguish dynamic neural overactivity from dystonia and fixed musculoskeletal limitation; individual decisions require qualified clinical evaluation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A child’s goal is to join classroom activities but seating is uncomfortable. Which first step best reflects PRM reasoning?

options.text: Order the most expensive wheelchair immediately
Clarify the child’s activity and participation goal, examine seating/environment and current equipment, and arrange appropriate team assessment
Focus only on muscle tone
Assume discomfort is behavioral

practiceQuestions.rationale: Equipment decisions should follow assessment of person, task, environment, goals and current supports, with follow-up; discomfort warrants respectful assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has persistent pain and orthostatic symptoms with school absence. What is the best initial educational formulation?

options.text: Symptoms are disproven if routine tests are normal
Use a validating, biopsychosocial assessment, consider a differential and coordinate appropriate referrals
Assume one diagnosis based on symptom pattern alone
Prescribe an exercise plan without assessment

practiceQuestions.rationale: PRM reasoning recognizes symptoms as real, avoids premature closure, and coordinates evaluation with relevant specialties; specific care is not provided here.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the accurate board-status statement for pediatric rehabilitation medicine?

options.text: There is no distinct board examination
ABPMR offers a PRM subspecialty certification examination with published eligibility pathways, including two years of ACGME PRM fellowship after PM&R residency
Completing an independent online course confers eligibility
Any one-year clinical placement automatically qualifies every candidate

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABPMR publishes a separate PRM exam and its prerequisites. Online study does not confer board eligibility; candidates must confirm current pathway-specific requirements directly.

title: Pediatric Residency Program
level: Clinical physician residency (independent educational course; not a residency)-aligned independent study

prerequisites.level: Advanced undergraduate/medical-student to early postgraduate self-study; this is not instruction that authorizes patient care.
required: Prior human biology, anatomy/physiology, biochemistry, microbiology, statistics and clinical examination foundations.
Ability to read evidence summaries and use age-specific units and reference ranges.
recommended: Completion of medical-school preclinical foundations and supervised clinical experience for contextual reading.
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e prerequisite refresh, especially development, cardiovascular, respiratory, renal and immune physiology.
prerequisites.notImplied: No physician credential, clinical competence, procedural skill, patient-care authorization, supervised experience or residency entry eligibility is conferred.

objectives: Use age-specific physiology and development to build a focused pediatric differential.
Map clinical questions to all 24 published ABP General Pediatrics domains and four universal tasks; explain the blueprint is not a prediction or pass guarantee.
Interpret preventive schedules, immunization resources and clinical guidelines with an explicit date/population check.
Recognize emergencies and red flags, state uncertainty, and describe when supervised escalation is required.
Communicate with children, adolescents and caregivers in a family-centered, developmentally appropriate and non-stigmatizing manner.
Use appropriate case-resource links without copying patient records or images, and verify license and attribution before any reuse.
Summarize evidence and propose a modest quality-improvement question without claiming causation from an uncontrolled observation.

units.assessment: Produce an age-specific prevention plan, cite the relevant schedule version and explain two contextual modifications.

rubric: 35% age-specific interpretation and no screen/diagnosis confusion

assignments.title: Fever and respiratory triage reasoning map
assignments.deliverable: Two fictional cases; represent data, check inclusion/exclusion, prioritize differential and explain escalation/uncertainty.

assignments.title: Adolescent confidential interview reflection
assignments.deliverable: Interview plan for a fictional scenario with confidentiality explanation, sensitive history and safety follow-up.

assignments.title: Pediatric evidence and QI mini-brief
assignments.deliverable: A one-page PICO-style clinical question plus a simulated process measure and a small test-of-change plan.

assignments.title: Integrated oral board-style synthesis
assignments.deliverable: Three original fictional vignettes spanning newborn, general pediatric and adolescent age groups; five-minute structured presentation per case.

assignment.grading: Suggested formative rubric only. No summative pass score, validated predictor, credential, examination equivalence or board-preparation guarantee.

components: 5 assignments assessed by transparent formative rubrics
Optional self-reflection on uncertainty and communication
assessment.criterion: Learners should be able to explain reasoning and identify limits; a self-study score does not establish clinical competence or exam readiness. No official ABP questions are reproduced.

officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official directory identifies Johns Hopkins Children’s Center, ACGME-accredited status and three-year duration. Public curriculum page describes PGY-1/2/3 supervision, progressive responsibility, ward, NICU, PICU, ED, primary care, subspecialty and elective experiences. It notes rotations may change with 2025 ACGME requirements. Global Health and Health Equity/Advocacy are described as resident pathways, not independent specialties or board categories. medical.programmeSourceScope: The packet names one Johns Hopkins School of Medicine clinical physician residency. The directory title “Pediatric Residency Program” corresponds to the Harriet Lane Pediatric Residency Program; the program-specific page explicitly reports ACGME accreditation and three years. Both names are preserved as the directory alias/formal program name, not counted as separate institutional variants. Hopkins Global Health and Health Equity/Advocacy are pathways within residency, not separate physician specialties or boards. The Physician Scientist Training Program (PSTP) is a research-oriented resident pathway with ARP, IRP and research-concentration variants; it is not a non-physician postdoctoral job, and it does not itself denote a distinct board exam. The ARP has a separate application/match and altered training sequence, but remains a physician-training pathway with ABP-specific eligibility requirements; this core curriculum does not claim to cover or qualify a trainee for it. ACGME combined Internal Medicine–Pediatrics is separately listed and is not the categorical Pediatrics programme in this packet. Hopkins All Children’s Hospital is a distinct institution/program and is not folded into this packet. No Harvard-affiliated variant was supplied in the official programme packet, and none is claimed.
sourceCaveats: Johns Hopkins pages summarize rotations and pathways but do not publish the full proprietary curriculum or full didactic timetable; no institution-provided hours were inferred.
The publicly linked ABP outline is the 2024 PDF and its landing page was updated 2025-11-25. Check for future revision before use. Domain weights do not guarantee exam content or passing.
CDC schedule page reviewed 2026-10-07 identifies its July 2, 2025 schedule as current; because recommendations and legal/policy context can change, revisit the page before clinical use.
AAP well-appearing febrile infant guidance is specific to its defined term 8–60-day population and enumerated exclusions; full text access may vary. This program is not a bedside clinical protocol.

Video runtimes come from public YouTube metadata queried on 2026-10-07, not a full audiovisual content audit. Public free-to-view access is distinct from permission to download, mirror, embed or reuse. External recordings remain hosted by source/uploader.

The course is not an official Johns Hopkins/Harvard curriculum, ACGME-accredited training, medical school degree, supervised clinical experience, clinical privileges, licensure, ABP eligibility, specialty certification, procedure competence or guarantee of passing.
Human clinical review is not performed. This version is an educational draft requiring qualified pediatric faculty review before any clinical teaching deployment.

Thin or absent coverage remains for outpatient prevention/growth and obesity; adolescent confidentiality/mental health; child safeguarding; dermatology, ophthalmology/ENT and orthopedics/sports medicine; genetics/dysmorphology; rheumatology; ethics, patient safety and QI; and guideline-current US practice. medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A well-appearing 18-day-old term infant has a documented rectal temperature of 38.1°C at home within the past day. What is the most important first step in applying the AAP febrile-infant guideline?

options.text: Apply the 29–60-day algorithm because the infant appears well.
Use the 8–21-day pathway only after confirming the infant meets inclusion criteria and has no exclusion requiring another approach.
Do not evaluate because the fever was measured at home.
Use the guideline for every infant younger than 90 days.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline covers well-appearing, term infants 8–60 days with qualifying rectal fever, with separate age strata. Confirm eligibility and exclusions before using an algorithm; an infant 18 days old falls in the youngest age band. This is educational, not a management order.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 5-year-old has a positive developmental screening questionnaire but no loss of skills. Which interpretation is best?

options.text: The result alone establishes a neurodevelopmental diagnosis.
Screening identifies concern and should lead to developmental surveillance, clinical evaluation and appropriate follow-up.
No further action is needed until school age.
Only a specialist may discuss the result with the family.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A screening test is not a diagnosis. Interpret in context, gather developmental/family information, evaluate concerns and arrange follow-up/referral as appropriate.

practiceQuestions.stem: A school-aged child with asthma presents with marked work of breathing and reduced air movement. Which reasoning priority is most appropriate?

options.text: A quiet chest proves the episode is improving.
Assess severity and ventilation/oxygenation, treat/escalate under local protocol, and reassess promptly.
Wait for spirometry before stabilizing.
Use oxygen saturation alone to determine disposition.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Reduced air movement with distress can indicate severe obstruction; immediate severity assessment and timely escalation/reassessment take priority. No single finding or saturation replaces clinical assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: A parent asks whether a child who missed early vaccine doses must restart the entire series. What is the best general response?

options.text: Most interrupted series are restarted from dose one.
Use the current CDC catch-up schedule and minimum intervals; do not assume a restart is needed.
Wait until the next annual visit.
Use the adult schedule because the series is late.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC schedule resources provide catch-up guidance and minimum intervals; the vaccine-specific schedule and history are required. Recommendations are date-sensitive.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 15-year-old requests time alone during a health visit. Which approach best supports adolescent care?

options.text: Refuse because a parent must be present for all questions.
Explain confidentiality and its limits before sensitive questions, then follow applicable law and safety obligations.
Promise complete confidentiality without exception.
Document only the parent’s answers.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Developmentally appropriate confidential care requires explaining privacy and its limits, including safety and reporting duties that depend on context/jurisdiction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 9-month-old has fever and a bag urine sample that grows bacteria. Which conclusion is most defensible before treatment decisions?

options.text: A bag culture always proves urinary infection.
Interpret the sample method and urinalysis; obtain an appropriately collected confirmatory specimen when indicated.
Ignore urine testing because infants rarely have UTI.
Diagnose pyelonephritis from culture alone.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Specimen method affects contamination and interpretation. Use age-appropriate guideline recommendations and clinical context; culture alone from a potentially contaminated specimen is not definitive.

practiceQuestions.stem: A term infant develops respiratory distress shortly after birth. Which framework best structures the initial differential?

options.text: Assume transient tachypnea if delivery was by cesarean.
Consider transition-related, pulmonary, infectious, cardiac and metabolic causes while assessing severity and perinatal context.
Rule out heart disease from a single normal pulse oximeter reading.
Wait for a chest radiograph before assessing airway and breathing.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Neonatal respiratory distress has a broad differential; immediate assessment/stabilization and context-guided evaluation precede diagnostic certainty.

practiceQuestions.stem: A child presents with a limp and fever. Which finding should most strongly increase urgency for evaluation of an invasive musculoskeletal infection?

options.text: Full painless range of motion and normal activity.
Inability to bear weight with focal joint pain and systemic illness.
A remote history of mild ankle sprain.
Pain only after prolonged sports practice that resolves with rest.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Fever with inability to bear weight and focal painful joint raises concern for time-critical septic arthritis/osteomyelitis; rapid clinical assessment and escalation are needed. It is a red flag, not a definitive diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: A child has pallor and fatigue. The only supplied result is a low hemoglobin. What is the best next reasoning step?

options.text: Diagnose iron deficiency without further context.
Assess age, indices, reticulocyte response, diet, symptoms and relevant history; then choose a focused differential and tests.
Assume malignancy.
Repeat hemoglobin in a year.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Anemia is a finding with multiple causes; indices, reticulocyte response, history and clinical status refine the differential and urgency.

practiceQuestions.stem: A resident notices that a clinic’s no-show rate is rising after appointment reminders changed. What is the most appropriate first quality-improvement step?

options.text: Assume the change caused the increase and roll it back everywhere.
Define the measure and population, examine baseline/trend and context, involve stakeholders, then test a small improvement with monitoring.
Report the result as a randomized trial.
Ignore it because it is not a clinical diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Q.I. begins with a clearly operationalized aim/measure, understanding the system and trends, engaging stakeholders and iteratively testing changes; observational change does not establish causality.

title: Pediatric Surgery
prerequisites: Medical-school level anatomy, physiology, pathology, pharmacology and evidence appraisal; preferably prior general-surgery knowledge for advanced learners.
This is a knowledge course, not an entry-to-practice course. Clinical fellowship applicants have separate institutional and board prerequisites.
objectives: Map pediatric surgery study to ABS QE content categories and dimensions without treating the blueprint as a full curriculum.
Reason through pediatric presentations across disease understanding, preoperative, perioperative and follow-up dimensions.
Use age-appropriate differential diagnosis, imaging stewardship, team escalation, safeguarding and multidisciplinary decision frameworks.
Critically appraise open educational sources and articulate evidence limitations, access, licensing and dates.
Distinguish institutional fellowship descriptions, ACGME standards, ABS certification rules and this independent course.

assignment.title: Integrated pediatric surgery case conference portfolio
assignment.prompt: For three educational case analyses, work through (1) a clearly labeled constructed fictional neonatal obstruction vignette, (2) the linked published pediatric trauma case report, and (3) the linked published late-presenting CDH case report. For published cases, separate reported facts from your inference and do not relabel actual facts as fictional. For each, state a differential, map to QE category and care dimension, cite current authoritative sources, discuss team/transfer and follow-up questions, and note what cannot be concluded. Do not copy images or patient records.

rubric.criterion: Safety, team, safeguarding and equity reasoning

assignment.limitations: Written educational assessment only; not validated; no clinical or procedural competence determination.

assessment.format: Low-stakes unit case exercises, 10 original multiple-choice questions and capstone portfolio; suggested self-check threshold 80% after review, not a passing standard.
assessment.blueprintAlignment: ABS 2023 QE blueprint categories: General Pediatric Surgery 55%, Critical Care 13%, Trauma 13%, Oncology 13%, General Pediatrics 6%; dimensions disease understanding 20%, preoperative 38%, perioperative 30%, follow-up/outcomes 12%; prenatal flag 5%, ambulatory 8% (flags may overlap care dimensions).
assessment.limitations: Questions are original for education, not official ABS exam content or predictive of examination outcomes.

topicGaps: No exact playback runtime could be independently observed for any accessible candidate in this expansion pass. The one new APSA neonatal vascular-access recording is relevant but excluded from hours; its caption end timestamp is not a verified runtime.

Verified accessible external video hours remain 0. The 36-hour floor remains an unfilled video gap; existing and newly authored scripts/plans are not rendered media and target minutes are not counted.

The SCORE 2026–2027 outline spans substantially more domains than the five authored episodes: airway and thoracic disease, congenital anomalies, colorectal/GU, critical care, trauma, oncology, endocrine/soft tissue/vascular anomalies, transplant, and follow-up still require topic-specific expansion and source review.

The neonatal obstruction source is a single-center retrospective study; it cannot establish universal epidemiology or comparative management effectiveness. The appendicitis guideline is from 2020 and requires current local reconciliation; the NCI PDQ update must be rechecked at use.
Institution-specific private didactics and complete rotation schedules remain unavailable in the accessed Johns Hopkins public pages.

medical.boardStatus: A distinct ABS pediatric surgery certificate exists. ABS states both PSQE and PSCE plus training requirements are required. PSITE is a program-administered in-training assessment, not a certification examination. Board process checked 2026-10-07; applicants must re-check current ABS policies.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent self-study course does not establish ABS or general surgery certification, board eligibility, examination admissibility, ACGME/RCPSC training, case logs, required operative experience, PALS completion, licensure, or procedure competence. ABS currently requires (among other conditions) accredited two-year fellowship, 96 weeks full-time clinical activity, general surgery certification, and verified fellowship operative reports; exact current rules control.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The packet names the Johns Hopkins Pediatric Surgery fellowship. Public source review revealed a distinct Baltimore/University of Maryland cooperative two-year program and a separate Johns Hopkins All Children’s two-year Florida fellowship. Both exact official variants retained; no Harvard offering was identified in the supplied packet. The All Children’s details should not be projected onto the Baltimore/UM program. Official institutional pages establish public descriptions, not the completeness of private curricula.

topicGaps: No exact playback runtime could be independently observed for any accessible candidate in this expansion pass. The one new APSA neonatal vascular-access recording is relevant but excluded from hours; its caption end timestamp is not a verified runtime.

Verified accessible external video hours remain 0. The 36-hour floor remains an unfilled video gap; existing and newly authored scripts/plans are not rendered media and target minutes are not counted.

The SCORE 2026–2027 outline spans substantially more domains than the five authored episodes: airway and thoracic disease, congenital anomalies, colorectal/GU, critical care, trauma, oncology, endocrine/soft tissue/vascular anomalies, transplant, and follow-up still require topic-specific expansion and source review.

The neonatal obstruction source is a single-center retrospective study; it cannot establish universal epidemiology or comparative management effectiveness. The appendicitis guideline is from 2020 and requires current local reconciliation; the NCI PDQ update must be rechecked at use.
Institution-specific private didactics and complete rotation schedules remain unavailable in the accessed Johns Hopkins public pages.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 10-year-old has migrating right lower quadrant pain and equivocal examination. When imaging is indicated, which is the preferred initial study in the pediatric pathway cited in WSES guidance?

options.text: Abdominal ultrasound
Routine standard-dose CT
Plain abdominal radiograph only
Diagnostic laparoscopy in every equivocal patient

practiceQuestions.rationale: Ultrasound is recommended as initial imaging for suspected pediatric appendicitis; decisions integrate clinical context and local expertise. Scores alone are not definitive.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional newborn has bilious emesis and abdominal distension. What is the best cognitive next step?

options.text: Treat as possible urgent obstruction/volvulus, stabilize and promptly involve pediatric surgery while evaluating
Assume physiologic reflux and discharge
Begin oral feeding trial before assessment
Wait for symptoms to persist for 24 hours

practiceQuestions.rationale: Bilious emesis in a neonate can signal time-sensitive obstruction; this is an educational prioritization prompt, not a treatment protocol.

practiceQuestions.stem: A stable child has a renal mass suspicious for Wilms tumor. Which is a sound planning principle?

options.text: Assess renal/abdominal imaging and chest staging and coordinate with pediatric oncology under the applicable protocol
Perform percutaneous biopsy in all cases without considering protocol
Assume imaging is pathognomonic and omit staging
Use PET as the only routine staging test

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI PDQ describes clinical/imaging workup and multidisciplinary, protocol-based care; exact management depends on protocol and findings.

practiceQuestions.stem: A preschool child has suspected appendicitis and a low clinical score. Which statement is best?

options.text: A low score cannot independently exclude disease; interpret history, exam, labs and imaging pathway
Scores are definitive across ages
Clinical scores replace reassessment
Only CT can establish diagnosis

practiceQuestions.rationale: Clinical scores have limitations, especially in young children; integrate age-specific presentation and diagnostic pathway.

practiceQuestions.stem: A child with major blunt trauma appears deceptively compensated but has worsening perfusion. What principle best applies?

options.text: Pediatric patients may compensate before rapid deterioration; reassess and mobilize team early
Normal blood pressure excludes shock
Use adult size assumptions for resuscitation
Defer team activation until hypotension

practiceQuestions.rationale: The linked educational trauma case and ABS outline emphasize pediatric trauma/critical care; local protocols govern care.

practiceQuestions.stem: In an educational safeguarding case, history and injury pattern raise concern but are not conclusive. What is the appropriate learning response?

options.text: Document objective findings, ensure immediate safety and use institutional safeguarding/reporting pathways
Confront the caregiver and independently determine culpability
Avoid consultation until certainty is established
Use a single imaging finding as proof

practiceQuestions.rationale: Possible maltreatment requires careful objective assessment and mandated local pathways; no single finding proves intent.

practiceQuestions.stem: An infant has prenatal CDH diagnosis. Which statement best characterizes counseling?

options.text: Discuss multidisciplinary planning, uncertainty and condition-specific options; do not imply a single fixed repair time
All infants undergo immediate repair at birth regardless of physiology
Prenatal imaging alone predicts individual outcome exactly
Fetal intervention is standard for all cases

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDH assessment and timing are condition- and physiology-specific; counsel with current specialist team and evidence.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about ABS pediatric surgery certification is correct?

options.text: Initial certification requires both the Pediatric Surgery QE and Certifying Exam after prerequisite training and general surgery certification
The PSITE alone confers board certification
There is no pediatric surgery-specific ABS certificate
Completing a self-study course grants eligibility

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABS lists distinct QE and CE as required and specifies accredited fellowship plus primary general surgery certification.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the most appropriate interpretation of the public Hopkins offerings?

options.text: Baltimore/University of Maryland cooperative program and Johns Hopkins All Children’s are distinct institutional tracks
All Children’s is just another name for the Baltimore fellowship
The All Children’s page proves identical rotations at both locations
A public directory entry alone defines board eligibility

practiceQuestions.rationale: The two official JH pages describe separate settings and program details; their public stated curricular facts should remain distinct.

practiceQuestions.stem: A child undergoing a fictional operation is recovering; a learning plan includes long-term function. Which ABS QE dimension is explicitly named?

options.text: Follow-up and outcomes
Only operative technique
Research productivity
Call schedule

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABS blueprint includes follow-up/outcomes (12%) as a dimension, alongside disease understanding, preoperative and perioperative care.

title: Pediatric Surgery Fellowship
prerequisites: Advanced physician-learning level: prior medical school and general-surgery foundation expected for full use; not an entry qualification or substitute for residency.
Basic pediatric physiology, anatomy, embryology, acute-care reasoning, evidence appraisal and research literacy.
Learners who are not licensed clinicians must use cases only for education, not clinical decision-making, patient care or procedural activity.
Use only public, lawfully accessed sources; do not copy patient data or images.
objectives: Organize pediatric surgical differential diagnosis and oral case reasoning across the current public SCORE topic list.
Map material to ABS public PSCE five-domain description while distinguishing it from protected content and undisclosed written-exam weighting.
Appraise uncertainty and guideline currency without turning a teaching case into a universal treatment pathway.
Recognize multidisciplinary, developmental, neonatal, emergency, oncologic and longitudinal care dimensions.
Use authentic case-image repositories as linked resources only and obey case-specific privacy and license conditions.
Explain why self-study hours cannot confer clinical competence, licensure, accreditation, board eligibility or certification.

units.title: Pediatric surgical scope, developmental physiology, and safe systems
objectives: Differentiate pediatric-surgery scope from other age-defined surgical specialties and subspecialty overlap.
Relate age/developmental stage and congenital history to risk assessment, uncertainty, and family-centered decisions.
Separate a teaching vignette from clinical decision authority.
topics: Surgical problems from fetal life through adolescence; transition to adult care; growth/development; family communication; consent/assent; ethics; disparities; multidisciplinary care; safety and handoff.
boardDomains: SCORE scope across categories; ABS board eligibility prerequisites; ACGME competencies, supervision and graduated responsibility.
units.casePractice: Build a one-page differential-first reasoning map and a family-centered handoff for a fictional referral.
units.assessment: 10-minute oral case: state knowns, missing data, urgency, consultant roles, uncertainty and escalation; rubric evaluates organization (40%), reasoning (30%), safety/limitations (20%), communication (10%).

units.title: Neonatal surgical physiology and the newborn with obstruction
objectives: Use developmental and physiologic context to organize the differential for neonatal obstruction.
Distinguish stabilization priorities from definitive diagnosis or operation; identify time-critical deterioration.
Interpret imaging descriptions cautiously and identify when source limitations matter.
topics: Embryology; transition from fetal circulation; neonatal shock; preterm physiology; radiographic patterns; atresia, malrotation/volvulus, meconium obstruction, NEC and perforation; resuscitation and transfer.
boardDomains: SCORE neonatal physiology, neonatal obstruction, intestinal atresia, malrotation, meconium ileus, NEC, neonatal gastric perforation; PSCE GI/hepatobiliary/abdomen, trauma/critical care.
units.casePractice: Use a constructed term newborn vignette with bilious emesis to list immediate information needed, differential, red flags, and team communication without prescribing individualized care.
units.assessment: Structured 5-minute oral response and annotated differential; rubric rewards urgency recognition, differential breadth, rationale, and no unsafe certainty.

boardDomains: SCORE gastroschisis, omphalocele, prenatal anomalies, neonatal physiology, nutrition; PSCE GI/abdomen and critical care.
