units.casePractice: Use a constructed cholestasis case to define key discriminating history/lab/imaging questions, referrals and uncertainty.
units.assessment: Problem representation + concept map; rubric: anatomy 25%, differential 25%, information gaps 20%, multidisciplinary issues 20%, citations 10%.

units.title: Head/neck, endocrine, GU and gynecologic surgery
objectives: Create safe differential frameworks for neck mass, endocrine lesion, acute scrotum and adnexal pain.
Recognize conditions requiring prompt evaluation and referral rather than reassurance from incomplete data.
Describe developmental, psychosocial, fertility, assent and multidisciplinary dimensions.
topics: Thyroglossal/branchial anomalies; thyroid/adrenal disease; undescended testis; torsion; disorders of sex development; ovarian torsion/mass; anorectal/urogenital anomalies; transition.
boardDomains: SCORE head/neck/endocrine/GU and ovarian/testicular topics; PSCE head/neck/endocrine/GU.
units.casePractice: Fictional acute scrotal-pain triage: identify missing facts and time-sensitive consultation need; no case-specific procedure instructions.
units.assessment: Oral response; rubric: recognition 35%, differential 25%, escalation 20%, communication/ethics 20%.

units.title: Thoracic, airway, and chest-wall surgery
objectives: Structure reasoning for respiratory distress with congenital thoracic pathology and airway symptoms.
Compare conceptual indications/risks and team needs for chest-wall disease, lung lesions and airway foreign body.
Avoid interpreting operative videos as adequate training or assuming universal indication.
topics: Pectus; congenital lung lesions; empyema; pneumothorax; vascular ring/sling; tracheomalacia; bronchoscopy concept; thoracic trauma; airway foreign bodies.
boardDomains: SCORE thoracic/airway/chest wall; PSCE thoracic/airway/chest wall.
units.casePractice: Use a linked, hospital-hosted surgical video only for observation; create a non-procedural pre-op/post-op concept checklist from public sources.
units.assessment: Brief plus 10-minute case discussion; rubric: recognition 30%, reasoning 30%, complications/limits 20%, consent/privacy 20%.

units.title: Evidence, QI, research literacy, ethics, and oral-board integration
objectives: Appraise guideline evidence and distinguish consensus, evidence level, institutional pathway, board standards and patient-specific decisions.
Present a clear structured answer with rationale, uncertainty, contingency plans and respect for limits.
Protect privacy and respect rights in authentic image/case learning.
topics: Guideline currency; QI; outcomes; bias; research consent; privacy and deidentification; trainee wellness; communication; end-of-life care; examination domains; professional limits.
boardDomains: SCORE outline and public PSCE domains; ACGME competencies; ABS does not disclose protected exam material.
units.casePractice: Prepare a fictional 15-minute oral board mini-case and a 1-page evidence-to-practice appraisal; do not use actual ABS questions or patient material.
units.assessment: Two blinded peer reviews using rubric: organization/rationale 25%, key findings 20%, evidence/uncertainty 20%, contingency/safety 20%, professionalism/communication 15%.

assignment.title: Fictional pediatric surgery case conference and evidence memo
assignment.instructions: Choose one fictional case prompt from Units 2–10. Submit a 1,000–1,500 word problem representation, prioritized differential, missing-information list, time-critical threats, multidisciplinary communication map, evidence appraisal, uncertainty statement, follow-up/contingency framework and oral presentation. Use citations from public sources. Do not include identifiable patient data, copied images, or treatment orders for a real person.

rubric.criterion: Safety, uncertainty, escalation, and scope limits

assignment.passingInterpretation: Educational formative rubric only; not validated, not a board predictor, not official ABS exam content.

assessment.format: 12 unit checks with original questions; end-of-course written/oral reasoning assignment and peer feedback.
assessment.scoring: Formative review against each assignment rubric; require revision of any unsafe certainty or unsupported clinical claim.
assessment.limits: No validated cut score or board-passing prediction. Questions are original study material, not official exam content. Human clinical review not performed.

unitMap.text: Pediatric surgical scope, developmental physiology, and safe systems
coveredTopics: Surgical problems from fetal life through adolescence; transition to adult care; growth/development; family communication; consent/assent; ethics; disparities; multidisciplinary care; safety and handoff.

unitMap.text: Neonatal surgical physiology and the newborn with obstruction
coveredTopics: Embryology; transition from fetal circulation; neonatal shock; preterm physiology; radiographic patterns; atresia, malrotation/volvulus, meconium obstruction, NEC and perforation; resuscitation and transfer.

unitMap.text: Abdominal wall defects: gastroschisis and omphalocele
coveredTopics: Prenatal counseling; delivery planning as multidisciplinary; stabilization; bowel assessment; closure strategies conceptually; feeding/TPN pathways; complex gastroschisis; omphalocele differentials/associated anomalies.

unitMap.text: Foregut, esophagus, diaphragm, and congenital thoracic disease
coveredTopics: CDH; esophageal atresia/TEF; congenital lung lesions; airway anomalies; reflux; mediastinal pathology; thoracic anatomy; fetal counseling and team-based postnatal care.

unitMap.text: Pediatric abdominal pain and acute appendicitis
coveredTopics: Appendicitis; mimics; imaging/radiation considerations; uncomplicated vs complicated disease; abscess/phlegmon; recurrence, follow-up, stewardship and QI.

unitMap.text: Hindgut, colorectal, and neonatal bowel disorders
coveredTopics: Hirschsprung disease/enterocolitis; anorectal malformation; NEC; short bowel; intestinal failure; inflammatory bowel disease; bowel atresias; long-term function, nutrition and family partnership.

unitMap.text: Pediatric surgical oncology and abdominal masses
coveredTopics: Neuroblastoma; Wilms tumor; hepatoblastoma; germ-cell tumors; adrenal, ovarian and testicular masses; lymphoma/leukemia overlap; biopsy/staging concepts; fertility and survivorship.

unitMap.text: Trauma, emergency surgery, and pediatric critical care
coveredTopics: Pediatric trauma; burns; blunt abdominal/thoracic injury; nonaccidental trauma safeguarding; sepsis; ECMO; ARDS; fluids/electrolytes; transfusion concepts; perioperative pain.

unitMap.text: Hepatobiliary, pancreas, spleen, and portal disease
coveredTopics: Biliary atresia; choledochal cyst; gallbladder disease; portal hypertension; hepatic infection/tumors; pancreatic disorders; splenic disease; transplant pathways.

unitMap.text: Head/neck, endocrine, GU and gynecologic surgery
coveredTopics: Thyroglossal/branchial anomalies; thyroid/adrenal disease; undescended testis; torsion; disorders of sex development; ovarian torsion/mass; anorectal/urogenital anomalies; transition.

unitMap.text: Thoracic, airway, and chest-wall surgery
coveredTopics: Pectus; congenital lung lesions; empyema; pneumothorax; vascular ring/sling; tracheomalacia; bronchoscopy concept; thoracic trauma; airway foreign bodies.

unitMap.text: Evidence, QI, research literacy, ethics, and oral-board integration
coveredTopics: Guideline currency; QI; outcomes; bias; research consent; privacy and deidentification; trainee wellness; communication; end-of-life care; examination domains; professional limits.

topicGaps: Four new unique, relevant free public recordings have observed channel-card runtimes and are counted: GICS Wilms tumor (3,724 s, Unit 7), GICS pediatric trauma webinar (5,461 s, Unit 8), pediatric laryngotracheal obstruction webinar (4,820 s, Unit 11; cross-specialty ENT), and GICS radiologic meeting (3,666 s, Unit 7). Together they provide 17671 seconds (4.9086 hours) of specialty-specific coverage. The existing Oxford lecture L01 remains uncounted because its exact runtime is unknown. The 36-hour target retains an actual gap of 31.0914 hours (1865.48 minutes).

APSA PedSurg.TV is confirmed as a public on-demand resource, but no complete item-by-item title, duration, access, and unit ledger was established here. Playlist hours remain uncounted; do not extrapolate a playlist total.

The publicly indexed GICS anorectal-malformation grand rounds is relevant to Unit 6 and has a displayed runtime of 1:02:27, but its YouTube watch page shows an age-restriction warning. It is excluded because unrestricted viewing without sign-in was not established; no restriction was bypassed.

No complete free public institutional pediatric-surgery lecture library was verified. Paid Oxford course material and subscription-only resources remain excluded. Short patient/family tutorials, procedure demonstrations, administrative talks, unrelated grand-rounds portions, and promotional content are not counted.

High-priority remaining source-backed teaching gaps include neonatal physiology and obstruction, abdominal wall defects, foregut/CDH, appendicitis evidence, neonatal bowel/Hirschsprung/intestinal failure, oncology beyond the Wilms and radiology sessions, trauma/critical care beyond one webinar, hepatobiliary disease, endocrine/GU, thoracic/airway beyond one ENT webinar, and evidence/ethics/oral reasoning. Six original episodes and six supplemental production plans remain scripted/planned only; they are not rendered, duration-probed, or counted.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Surgery (ABS) — Pediatric Surgery initial certification (PSQE and PSCE)
American Board of Surgery (ABS) — General Surgery primary certification (prerequisite)
medical.boardStatus: Pediatric surgery is a physician surgical subspecialty with an ABS initial-certification pathway; not a generic directory category or research-only/non-physician supplement. ABS requires completion of ACGME- or RCPSC-accredited pediatric surgery training and primary ABS general surgery certification, followed by both the Pediatric Surgery Qualifying Examination and Certifying Examination. There is no separate independent pediatric-surgery certifying board organization; ABS awards the certificate. PSITE is an in-training assessment, not a required board certification exam.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Self-study confers no board eligibility. As checked 2026-10-07, the ABS requires accredited 2-year pediatric-surgery training, general-surgery certification, unrestricted licensure requirements as specified, and other current application rules; applicants must re-check ABS policies at application. The ABS PSQE/PSCE are required for initial pediatric surgery certification. This educational course cannot satisfy any training, case log, PALS, licensure or eligibility requirement. [R6-R10]

medical.programmeSourceScope: Institution pages verify that these three exact clinical physician fellowship offerings are listed and support only the summarized public features. ACGME sets accreditation requirements (current document effective 2026-07-01); it is not a hospital schedule or board exam blueprint. ABS verifies separate board pathway and examinations. SCORE 2026–27 is the public training topic outline, not PSQE topic-weighted blueprint. Oxford course page describes paid residential course, not free lecture library. No generic directory category, research-only postdoctoral position, or non-physician supplement is silently treated as this physician specialty.

medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional 2-day-old has bilious emesis and abdominal distension. What is the safest initial reasoning approach for a trainee discussion?

options.text: Assume uncomplicated reflux and observe without escalation.
Treat as a potentially time-sensitive obstruction, assess stability and urgently involve the appropriate pediatric surgical/neonatal team while defining differential and needed data.
Diagnose malrotation from the symptom alone and prescribe an operation.
Wait for a specific imaging result before assessing stability.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Bilious emesis in a neonate is a red-flag presentation requiring urgent assessment and escalation; a vignette alone cannot establish a diagnosis. The reasoning sequence must begin with stability and time-critical differentials, not diagnostic certainty or a fixed procedure.

practiceQuestions.stem: A term newborn with apparently uncomplicated gastroschisis is stable. Which statement best represents the 2024 APSA guideline abstract?

options.text: Standardized gastroschisis nutrition and postnatal protocols are recommended, but comparative evidence is limited and length-of-stay effect is not consistent.
All babies require the same operative timing and closure technique.
The guideline proves protocols reduce mortality in all patients.
The guideline applies equally to complex gastroschisis and omphalocele.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline review found evidence levels 2–5, recommends gastroschisis-specific feeding and clinical-care protocols, and reports that length-of-stay reduction is not consistent. It concerns uncomplicated gastroschisis and does not mandate one closure technique.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional child with perforated appendicitis and a localized abscess, which interpretation is best supported by the open review?

options.text: A single management path is proven superior for every child.
Both immediate operation and nonoperative treatment are discussed; evidence limitations and context mean no universal answer follows from the vignette.
Interval appendectomy is always mandatory.
Antibiotics alone always prevent recurrence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The review describes competing operative and nonoperative approaches and notes ongoing controversy and paucity of high-quality comparative studies. Clinical care follows current local expert pathways, not a universal answer derived from a short case.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which ABS initial pediatric-surgery certification path is accurate?

options.text: Pass the PSITE only.
Pass the pediatric surgery PSQE and PSCE after meeting training requirements and primary general-surgery certification.
Pass an independent pediatric surgery board exam unrelated to ABS.
Complete a 36-hour course to become board eligible.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABS requires primary general-surgery certification and completion of accredited pediatric-surgery training; successful PSQE and PSCE are both required. PSITE is an in-training exam and not a certification requirement.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which topic domains are explicitly listed for the ABS Pediatric Surgery Certifying Examination?

options.text: Only written oncology and trauma questions.
Oncology; trauma/critical care; GI, hepatobiliary, abdomen; head/neck, endocrine, GU; thoracic, airway, chest wall.
General surgery only, with no pediatric-specific domains.
Surgical research, administration and pathology only.

practiceQuestions.rationale: These are the five public 30-minute oral-session subject areas listed by ABS. This course maps to them but does not reproduce or predict protected exam content.

practiceQuestions.stem: What does the current ACGME pediatric surgery requirement state for program length?

options.text: 12 months total.
24 months, with 48 weeks in each year comprising clinical pediatric surgery.
36 months of video viewing.
The requirement is not specified.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACGME 2026 requirements state the educational program is 24 months, with 48 weeks in each of two years comprising clinical pediatric surgery. This is an accredited clinical training rule, not a self-study-hour equivalence.

practiceQuestions.stem: A family asks whether a public operative video certifies them or a learner to reproduce the procedure. What is the best answer?

options.text: Yes, if watched twice.
No; it is an observational educational resource and does not establish supervised competence, authorization, credentialing or procedural readiness.
Yes, if accompanied by a quiz.
It replaces institutional training if the case appears uncomplicated.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Openly viewable recordings do not confer procedural competence, supervised experience, credentialing or license. The course is independent self-study and cannot replace accredited training.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description correctly distinguishes institutional programme descriptions from ACGME standards?

options.text: A hospital web page is the board blueprint.

A publicly described fellowship and its rotations are institution-specific facts; ACGME requirements are accreditation standards and neither automatically publishes a full curriculum or exam weighting.
The SCORE topic list is a complete hospital schedule.
A case-volume page guarantees every fellow meets a minimum.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Programme pages, ACGME requirements and board materials are different evidence types. They have different scopes and should not be collapsed into a claim of public full curriculum or board blueprint.

practiceQuestions.stem: A student identifies a linked patient image in an educational repository and wants to copy it to a course deck. What is the correct next step?

options.text: Copy because freely viewable means unrestricted.
Check the individual image’s deidentification and license/terms, obtain any required permissions, and otherwise link only; never rehost it.
Remove the caption and assume deidentification is complete.
Use any image if patient age is not shown.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free access is not a license. HHS describes HIPAA de-identification methods; repository case/image terms are item-specific. This project links resources and copies no patient images or records.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which conclusion about the 2026–27 SCORE pediatric surgery outline is accurate?

options.text: It is an exact public PSQE question weighting blueprint.
It is a patient-care curriculum outline with topics spanning the training program, not a published weighting scheme for the written board exam.
It lists only procedures and excludes nonoperative care.
It replaces ABS eligibility requirements.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABS describes SCORE as a list of topics to be covered in training. Public ABS exam information describes format but does not provide item-level or topic-weighted protected exam content.

boardNames: American Board of Urology (ABU)—general Urology certification (required prerequisite for pediatric subspecialty certification)
American Board of Urology (ABU)—Pediatric Urology Subspecialty Certification Examination (PSCE)
medical.boardStatus: Boston Children’s Hospital names the Alan B. Retik Pediatric Urology Fellowship as a two-year ACGME-accredited physician fellowship. ABU maintains a distinct Pediatric Urology subspecialty certification and exam; it is not a separate entry-level primary specialty board. No other institution or combined fellowship track is claimed in this item. ABU’s 2026 public page states the PSCE is offered every other year and lists October 22–24, 2026; as of the 2026-10-07 check, this is forthcoming. The 2026 ABU detailed content page was blocked by a cookie challenge; no question weighting is asserted. ABU describes broad examination content, including congenital abnormalities, childhood-acquired urologic problems and adolescent overlap.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Not eligible for board certification by completing this independent course. ABU states candidates must hold a current unrestricted general ABU urology certificate, practice pediatric urology, complete at least 24 months in an approved pediatric urology program, meet practice/log/CME requirements and pass its examination. Current 2026 requirements may change; the ABU candidate handbook is the controlling source. Never interpret this notice as individualized eligibility advice.

officialProgrammes.name: Alan B. Retik Fellowship Program in Pediatric Urology
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page calls it a two-year ACGME-accredited program: first year is clinical; second year offers clinical/health services, basic or translational research choices; optional third research year. Publicly listed conferences include weekly urology/radiology conference, indications conference, grand rounds, monthly journal club and M&M. Public admissions page does not publish every lecture schedule, rotation allocation or didactic-hour total. Its volume figures are institution-reported service statistics, not an individual fellow’s operative case count or competency guarantee.

medical.programmeSourceScope: MED-180 packet supplied only this Boston Children’s programme. It is an actual physician fellowship, not a generic directory category or research-only postdoctoral/non-physician track. The hospital is identified as a Harvard Medical School teaching hospital; that relationship does not make this course an official Harvard program. No separate institutional pediatric urology programme at Johns Hopkins is represented in this exact assignment packet or claimed here. No institutional variants or combined programme are inferred.
sourceCaveats: ABU official page lists a separate Pediatric Urology Subspecialty Certification, but its detailed exam content page returned a cookie-security gate. We use no official weighting or leaked questions. The ABU 2026 handbook PDF exists publicly; rely on ABU for current candidate requirements and confirm updates directly.

Boston Children’s institutional page is the sole exact programme variant provided in the MED-180 packet. Fellowship-specific curriculum pages do not disclose all lectures, exact didactic contact hours, rotations, individual fellow cases or outcomes. Self-reported volume totals must not be attributed as personal fellow case volume.
ACGME program requirements are standards for accredited graduate medical education, not a board exam blueprint or a set of online lessons.
The public CHOP course is a historic presentation/deck; not an actual counted video recording.

UCSF PedsUroFLO official page states lectures went on hiatus Jan 1, 2021 and past recordings are not CME. YouTube playlist runtimes are directly observed, but each media item may disappear/change; ledger records playlist page as duration evidence. The lectures are not necessarily fully aligned with 2026 practice.

AUA VUR guideline is published 2010/amended 2017; AUA cryptorchidism resource says validity confirmed 2025. Use current guideline sources and do not treat old recommendation text as current without rechecking.

EAU 2026 guidance is free for personal educational reading; EAU prohibits reproduction or external reposting absent written permission. Resource links are provided; no guideline text or figures are mirrored here.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 4-month-old with antenatal bilateral urinary tract dilation has a poor urinary stream, rising creatinine and a distended bladder. Which response best reflects a safe reasoning priority?

options.text: Assume benign physiologic dilation and schedule routine follow-up.
Recognize possible lower urinary tract obstruction and escalate urgent specialist/neonatal evaluation with renal/bladder assessment.
Diagnose posterior urethral valves from symptoms alone.
Order CT as the universal first study.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The presentation raises concern for clinically consequential obstruction and renal compromise; a differential and prompt multidisciplinary evaluation are appropriate. Do not assert a definitive diagnosis before evaluation; modality selection depends on context and radiation-sparing principles.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 2-year-old has recurrent febrile UTI and documented VUR. What should the learner add before framing an intervention question?

options.text: Ignore bowel symptoms because VUR fully explains recurrence.
Assess bladder-bowel/voiding symptoms, prior infection course, renal status and family priorities.
Conclude surgery is mandatory for every reflux grade.
Use reflux grade alone as proof of renal scarring.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Risk and decision-making in VUR are contextual. Bowel/voiding comorbidity, infection history, renal findings and preferences matter; a grade does not itself establish scarring or dictate the only intervention.

practiceQuestions.stem: A newborn has an undescended testis. Which statement best supports counseling?

options.text: A normal ultrasound excludes an intra-abdominal testis.
Evaluation is age-sensitive and counseling should acknowledge fertility and malignancy risks without implying orchiopexy removes all future risk.
Hormone therapy is universally required.
All such infants have a DSD.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AUA cryptorchidism resource and EAU chapter can be consulted for evolving guidance. Treatment can reduce but not eliminate later sequelae; avoid claims not warranted by evaluation.

practiceQuestions.stem: An adolescent with urinary urgency, constipation and daytime wetting is being discussed at clinic. Which framework is most useful?

options.text: Assess bowel, voiding and developmental context and characterize storage/emptying before assigning a cause.
Label this as anatomic obstruction without testing.
Assume symptoms are intentional.
Treat all symptoms as nocturnal enuresis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Symptom characterization and bowel history reduce premature closure; evaluation should fit age, red flags and clinical context.

practiceQuestions.stem: A child with myelomeningocele is transitioning to adult care. Which outcome set best reflects comprehensive follow-up?

options.text: Continence alone.
Renal protection, bladder/bowel function, independence, sexual health, psychosocial needs and continuity preferences.
Surgical history alone.
Urodynamic data without patient priorities.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Neuro-urology follow-up is multidisciplinary and life-course oriented; no single surrogate captures all outcomes.

practiceQuestions.stem: A newborn has atypical genital anatomy and possible DSD. What is the best initial communication principle?

options.text: Assign a definitive diagnosis from external appearance alone.
Use respectful, non-stigmatizing language and coordinate urgent multidisciplinary evaluation while protecting family privacy.
Promise a specific sex assignment before evaluation.
Defer all discussion until genetic results.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME expects multidisciplinary care and counseling in DSD. The learner should avoid diagnostic certainty or decisions based solely on an appearance descriptor.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the most appropriate interpretation of a public robotic operative video in a self-study course?

options.text: Completion proves operative competence.
Observation supports conceptual familiarity but cannot establish supervised case experience, judgment or procedural competence.
It substitutes for ACGME case log requirements.
It makes credentialing unnecessary.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME training requires supervised clinical education and case logging. Video observation cannot substitute for technical assessment or credentialing.

practiceQuestions.stem: When weighing follow-up imaging in a child with urinary tract dilation, what should a learner explicitly include?

options.text: Modality limits, clinical question, age, radiation/sedation considerations and whether a trend changes the next step.
Always repeat CT to maximize detail.
Ignore ultrasound because it is noninvasive.
Treat any imaging classification as independent of clinical findings.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Imaging choice should answer a clinical question while weighing modalities and pediatric safety risks; the ACGME requirements explicitly include imaging and safety.

practiceQuestions.stem: A published pediatric urology case report contains an image useful for teaching. Which action respects rights and privacy?

options.text: Copy it into the course because it is free to view.
Link to the source and verify article-specific reuse license, consent and de-identification before any reuse.
Remove the watermark and attribute verbally.
Assume open access means public domain.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Access and reuse rights differ; image reuse must follow the exact article license and appropriate patient consent/deidentification. The course never mirrors cases or images.

practiceQuestions.stem: A proposed quality project counts pyeloplasty as its sole endpoint for antenatal urinary tract dilation. What is the strongest critique?

options.text: Procedure occurrence is a surrogate and may not capture renal function, symptoms, patient burden or natural history.
It is necessarily an objective measure of cure.
Surgery should be the goal for all dilation.
It eliminates follow-up.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Meaningful outcome measures should reflect patient-centered and renal outcomes; PedsUroFLO includes a lecture explicitly critiquing pyeloplasty as a study endpoint.
